      "observations": [
        "All four owned file diffs were read. The landing adds an 86-line Lit Storybook example, 120 CSS lines and three Fluent body IDs, and changes GECKO_HEAD_REF from default to a literal revision. No production template/controller registration or test/assertion change is part of this original landing.",
        "The original story has three label-wrapped radios with name account-type and imap/microsoft/pop3 values. Its recommended class controls the badge, and the CSS depends on the actual input:checked state for card shadow and header/icon colors. The story passes its checked argument through an element-position interpolation, not a literal checked attribute or explicit ?checked binding; Lit renderer semantics were not paired, so successful initial selection/rendering is not inferred.",
        "Review inlines 1631944 and 1632113 question the div inside a span and acknowledge that concern. The selected original story still literally places the icon div inside the header span at lines 43–44. The concern is not shown adopted in the owned markup despite Done and acceptance. The original story is absent at fixed accepted; later production markup instead has empty-alt img icons within the header spans.",
        "The original CSS sets a 148 px by 127 px card, 56 px/69 px content rows, a 57 px header, 3 px body padding, min-inline-size:0 and overflow-wrap:anywhere. Brand/base tokens drive colors and 20% fills. These values support bounded layout-source facts, not a measured 127 px rendered total, locale fit, contrast or complete focus behavior. No card focus-state selector is added in this owned block.",
        "The fixed accepted production form uses later protocol-select class/name identifiers and a literal IMAP checked attribute. Its actual controller maps exchange/ews/graph to microsoft, selects a matching or fallback IMAP radio and reads input:checked. The current CSS differs in input hit-area/pointer handling and spacing; it is a later phase, not proof that the original Storybook interpolations or every control behaved the same.",
        "The three new Fluent IDs retain their values and have exact current template consumers. Current CSS has a local use-design-tokens exception around the card block; that is scoped configuration, not permission to export hard-coded sizing as a global style rule.",
        "Primary c4 attributes the pin to an accidental widget landing and c5 records the reset. The original source really pins 892b1a338388282b83cf4a2b2aa3153acad70263, while fixed accepted uses default. That later reset and its future source audit are separate; no Gecko build or compatibility result is inferred.",
        "Full original Root primary and B own-review collector scopes are available and will be joined without duplicate whole-discussion reading. Actual source facts decide adoption; historical Try/design/screenshot statements remain attributed and no Storybook/native/a11y run was performed.",
        "Complete original Root Bug 2028456 and B D301590 collector coverage is reused under its exact original IDs, readers, times and scopes. Only the three actual inline concerns and relevant general design/pin responses are reconciled here; there is no second whole-discussion coverage claim.",
        "Actual inline 1631944 questions div-in-span example markup; author inline 1632113 agrees it matters for the intended example, and the reviewer accepts with that comment to resolve. The selected source still contains the div inside the header span at lines 44–45. This request is not demonstrated adopted in the owned landing. Current production's img inside span is a later source phase, not evidence of original adoption.",
        "Actual inline 1639678 asks whether CSS imports duplicate messenger.xhtml imports. The selected owned CSS hunk adds the card block without changing the import list, and the story retains explicit CSS imports. No substantive reply proving a final import policy is present in the retained thread; no global deduplication mandate or import-cost result is inferred.",
        "The design request names total/top/bottom dimensions, long-text drift/padding, badge sizing and token fills. The author updates the revision and says other issues are addressed while asking about badge dimensions. Later edited acceptance attributes the apparent total-height discrepancy to the border, reports corrected padding/badge spacing, and says icons were confirmed through a screenshot while Storybook had issues. Those are historical reports. The selected CSS provides exact declarations, including 127 px card height, 56 px/69 px grid rows, 57 px header, 3 px body padding, min-inline-size:0, overflow-wrap:anywhere and 20% token-based fills; no measured geometry or complete visual/a11y outcome is claimed.",
        "Primary c4 explicitly calls the Gecko ref pin accidental and c5 records the later reset. The selected owned change truly pins the literal revision; fixed accepted default is a separate endpoint. No body from the later unassigned reset landing has been studied and no successful paired Gecko build is inferred."
